item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports separating item relationships rather than treating every useful neighbor as similar. [TransGAT (ICDM 2024)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10884336/) couples complement and substitute graphs, encodes behavioral direction, and adds self-supervised augmentation. [MMSC (2025; revised 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.22268) combines relation-aware representations with self-supervised denoising to address noisy behavior-derived associations and sparse items. Its foundation-model and multimodal components exceed this benchmark’s constraints; the transferable ideas are separate relation channels, structured relation paths, and confidence-weighted supervision. Interaction sequences alone do not establish whether two items are substitutes or complements.\n\nFor text-based sequential modeling, [JEPA4Rec (COLM 2025)](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=0Qbwjd0fxB) combines language modeling of item descriptions with predictive representation learning; its abstract describes reduced reliance on large-scale pretraining, which does not establish a lightweight, entirely scratch-trained recipe. [CALRec (2024)](https://research.google/pubs/calrec-contrastive-alignment-of-generative-llms-for-sequential-recommendation/) aligns sequence and item text representations contrastively, but relies on pretrained PaLM-2. A feasible adaptation—an engineering proposal, not a reported result—is a randomly initialized token-embedding mean-pool encoder over permitted titles/descriptions, fused with SASRec item IDs. Build separate sparse graphs for textual similarity and directed training-sequence transitions; learn relation-specific projections with edge reconstruction and text–interaction alignment losses. Treat these as similarity and transition channels until relation labels exist. Gate their contributions by sequence context, retain the ID residual, and select changes using the stipulated macro validation HR@10."}
